"Suíshū: Treatise on Music."
"Yuèfǔ Shījí" Volume Nine.
"Shī Jì" Volume One Hundred Nineteen.
"Huángxià: Offering to the Imperial High Ancestor"
Auspicious lineage, a thousand layers of excellence,
vast source, ten thousand miles long.
In times of obscurity, still folding wings,
in the way of virtue, thus concealing light.
Great virtue surely has descendants,
benevolence and righteousness ultimately flourish.
The bright star first initiates blessings,
the great lightning long displays auspicious signs.
○ Same as above.
"Huángxià: Offering to the Imperial Great-Grandfather, the Virtuous Emperor"
Flourishing, shining upon the lofty achievements,
sage foundation, harmonious western borders.
Exalting benevolence, crossing the Wèi high,
accumulating virtue, covering the Jūyuán.
The imperial chart displays past traces,
the royal enterprise prospers from former honor.
Renewed fragrance in the Déyáng Temple,
layered blessings in the Shòulíng Garden.
A hundred spirits shine upon ancestral deeds,
a thousand years of blessings for filial descendants.
○ Same as above.
"Huángxià: Offering to the Imperial Grandfather, the Great Ancestor, the Civil Emperor"
Majestic plans belong to heaven's creation,
grand strategies encounter soaring multitudes.
Wind and clouds still heed commands,
the dragon leaps, seizing opportunity.
A hundred and two hold heavenly peril,
three parts resist joyful acclaim.
Hángǔ's wind and dust disperse,
Héyáng's mists clear.
Aiding the weak, fallen customs rise,
supporting the endangered, declining fortunes return.
The earth's pivot collapses yet is righted,
heaven's axis falls but is pursued again.
The plain altar suddenly transcends,
the Bì mound perhaps faintly endures.
Finally enfeoffed with a three-foot sword,
forever rolling up a warrior's robe.
○ Same as above.
"Huángxià: Offering to the Civil and Illustrious Empress Dowager"
The moon spirit arises in celebration,
sand auspices emerge from the source.
Merit matches Yǔ's traces,
virtue praises Yáo's gate.
Speech and demeanor follow rites,
the yúdí robe bears elegant patterns.
Form and appearance warm with virtue,
fair fame shines in Zhāoyáng.
Sun and moon do not linger,
seasons and years grow late.
Auspicious clouds entwine the heart,
the secluded palace is ever distant.
○ Same as above.
"Huángxià: Offering to Emperor Mǐn"
The dragon chart bases on succeeding virtue,
heaven's steps belong to hardship.
Songs of praise return, receiving auspicious signs,
yielding and deferring, then ascending the altar.
Ascending the carriage, thorns weigh heavy,
entering position, leaning on passes, cold.
Rolling and unfolding, clouds flood,
wandering and soaring, sunlight gradually fades.
Leaving Zhèng, never to return,
residing in Tóng, ultimately not coming back.
Sacrificing to Xià, now only the old,
honoring the spirit, posthumous title further pursued.
○ Same as above.
"Huángxià: Offering to Emperor Míng"
Like meeting the descending lord at Ruòshuǐ,
belonging to Wéizhèng at Qióngsāng.
Great indeed, guiding the imperial register,
majestic, facing heaven's mandate.
Just establishing the five-cloud offices,
first harmonizing the eight-wind commands.
Wénchāng's aura like pearls,
the Grand Historian's river like a mirror.
The southern palace's learning already opened,
the eastern tower's books still gathered.
Literary phrases, the rhythm of metal and stone,
brush and ink, wind and whirlwind upright.
The pure chamber's cassia abundant,
the Qí room's mushrooms flourishing.
Rather think of jade pipe flutes,
in vain see spirit garments dance.
○ Same as above.
"Huángxià: Offering to the High Ancestor, the Martial Emperor"
Southern rivers exhale cloud-breath,
The Northern Dipper sends down stars and celestial dust.
All spirits revere virtue,
Once in a thousand years, a sage appears.
When writings are complete, the Purple Tenuity stirs,
When laws are fixed, the phoenix is tamed.
Six armies are commanded to the western lands,
On the jiǎzǐ day, arrayed at the eastern neighbor.
Once armored robes are thus settled,
For ten thousand miles, no more dust arises.
Mist and clouds share five colors,
Sun and moon bear double halos.
The Flowing Sands are quiet in the west,
The Coiling Tree again serves in the east.
Joyful music hears the scarlet wild goose,
Náo songs see the white qílín.
Now as sacrifice for the six dynasties,
Still we welcome guests from Jiǔyí.
○Same as above.
Huángxià – Drinking the Blessing Wine
〈Huángxià – Drinking the Blessing Wine〉
Rites complete with libation and offering,
Music peaks, rest achieved.
Chánglí shines ahead,
Ancestral sacrifice, culture bright.
Strained wine floats with orchids,
Clear vessels hold fragrant herb wine.
Bowed like chime-stones, ritual decorum,
Circling round, spiritual blessings.
Receiving blessings, clearing the stands,
Drinking the blessing wine, moving the goblets.
Only glorious, only mighty,
Literate sons, literate grandsons.
○Same as above.
〈Huángxià – Returning to the Side Hall〉
The courtyard ends the four beginnings,
The mat concludes three offerings.
Looking back, stepping on the stairs,
Lingering over the remaining libations.
Six dragons raise their heads,
Seven elite guards alert the road.
Drums shift, the water-clock moves,
Winds turn, the wind-vane spins.
Reverently attending to affairs,
Continuously through the four seasons.
May the spirits bestow blessings,
Forever preserve them.
○Same as above.
〈Zhāoxià – Inviting the Spirits〉
Pitch in Jiázhōng,
Robes of dark dragon-emblems.
Profound and pure thoughts,
Enduring and far-reaching.
Approaching sacrifice at the union,
Ranking spirits by their origin.
Coming to court in order,
Assisting sacrifice with decorum.
Music and dance of six dynasties,
Guests sing of two kings.
Harmonious bells mark the rhythm,
Jingling bridle ornaments.
Qí palace offers jade dishes,
Fragrant cups float with gold.
Dòngtíng’s bells and drums,
Lóngmén’s zithers and lutes.
The music has transformed,
Only the spirits are present.
○From “Yǔ Zǐshān Collection” seven.
“Collection of Music Bureau Poems” nine.
“Guǎng Wénxuǎn” eleven.
“Shī Jì” one hundred nineteen.
〈Raising Songs – Offering Jade and Silk〉
Spirits are manifest in thought,
Without speaking, they command.
The rite of jade and silk,
Dare I present with solemn reverence.
Holding as if unable to bear it,
Offering as if receiving a mandate.
Interacting with the divine spirits,
Sincere in word and deed.
○Same as above.
〈Zhōu Five-Tone Modulation Songs〉
Preface says:
At the yuánzhēng banquet, the grand rite,
Guests arrive, food is presented,
Cups raised, jade offered.
Six pitches follow in harmony,
Eight winds flow freely.
To sing of great achievements,
To dance for success accomplished.
〈Gōng Modulation Songs – Five Pieces〉
Qì divided clear and turbid,
Origin opened, heaven and earth split.
Three powers first distinguished rightly,
Six positions began to form patterns.
Succeeding heaven, thus establishing elders,
Pacifying the people, then setting up rulers.
Their brightness vast as the sun,
Their grace thick as clouds.
Only in the past, our cultural ancestor,
Quelled chaos, resisted ballads.
Three parts not yet embracing fortune,
Eight hundred not crossing the river.
Rites spread, all under heaven trust,
Music corrected, spirits and people harmonized.
Dust of war ceases its alarms,
Rivers and seas wish to be waveless.
○From “Yǔ Zǐshān Collection” seven.
“Collection of Music Bureau Poems” fifteen.
“Shī Jì” one hundred nineteen.
Our emperor inherits from lower martiality,
Revolution lies in sovereign rule.
Corresponding to charts, matching Shùn’s jade,
Continuing virtue, receiving Yáo’s qín.
Chén Shǒu often deduced fate,
Yángchéng possessed a yielding heart.
Approaching the sun, early knowing distance,
Observing the abyss, early seeing depth.
Mysterious essence truly entrusted to drive,
The azure principle then all balanced.
Beginning the calendar, receiving myriad states,
Year’s auspice, celebrating all spirits.
Jade and silk all observe rites,
Huá and Róng each in court.
Phoenix resonance matches yízé,
Astronomy aligns with the jade balance.
Imperial foundation self-preserved by heaven,
All things then follow gēng.
○Same as above.
Grasping balance, leveling earth’s order,
Observing phenomena, rectifying celestial pivot.
Auspicious signs gather in Chìxiàn,
Divine omens shine in the imperial capital.
Again receiving Zhāohuá jade,
Still draped with orchid-leaf charts.
Golden waves bring the white rabbit,
Ruò River descends with azure crow.
Jade Dipper harmonizes origin,
Golden sands enrich the state’s taxes.
Qīngqiū still pacifies gardens,
Dānxué again nests with phoenixes.
Ānlè newly completes celebration,
Long life, a hundred blessings tally.
○Same as above.
Brightly ordered the nine clans,
Reverently the four gates host guests.
Yīnlíng submits northward,
Coiling Tree leads eastern ministers.
Ravine paths seek board-builders,
Stream sources take fishing lines.
Many scholars return to worthy relatives,
Fortified cities belong to close kin.
Noble rank links the Southern Dipper,
High glory rests on the Northern Star.
Welcoming seasons, thus推算 fate,
Managing duties, and ranking spirits.
Where sun and moon shine,
Where frost and dew evenly fall.
Forever following unified script and tracks,
Long without outsiders at the door.
○Same as above.
Lush and winding, beams and eaves stretch,
Lofty and towering, rivaling “Great Strength.”
Arched wood instructs the forest regulator,
Full model summons the catalpa craftsman.
Thousands of brackets like colored wings float,
Hundreds of arches like long rainbows resist.
Northward lies the road to Hándān,
Southward comes the view of Yǎnshī.
Dragon-head bears patterned ridgepoles,
Cloud lintels support martial canopies.
Dwellers do not seek narrowness,
Humble palaces, how hard to esteem?
Magnificent for all under heaven to behold,
Thus following Xiāo Hé’s example.
○Same as above.
〈Biàngōng Modulation – Two Pieces〉
The emperor, like light emerging from thunder, roams;
The sovereign, bright and skilled, resides in the trigram Li.
The lofty corridors alone receive his care and gaze,
Reverently he follows, still embracing non-action.
The dragon’s lair is not hard to approach,
The phoenix’s nest one may wish to peer into.
Jùcí should not be far away,
Fényáng—how could it be worth following?
The masses, sowing and planting, bear heavy burdens;
Canals and ditches, toil and labor are many.
The mulberry woods still pour down rain,
Accumulated stones thus open the river’s course.
Clear signs meet with eternal destiny,
Orderly measures encounter years of harmony.
Moreover, there is the “Song of the Warm Wind,”
Just now we hear the “Dew at Dawn” chant.

From *Collection of Music Bureau Poems*, scroll fifteen.

Transforming customs, broadening the Xuān calendar,
Exalting virtue, flourishing the Táng years.
Completing writings, reviving the great elegance,
Going forth in comfort, moving the music of heaven.
The yellow bell, the six pitch-standards correct,
The heavenly gate, the eight winds proclaimed.
Lone bamboo tunes the yang pipes,
Empty mulberry regulates the elegant strings.
In the dancing grove, phoenixes descend again,
On the singing mountain, phoenixes wish to come forth.
Hearing the tones, one can discern customs,
Listening to the tunes, then one thinks of worthies.
Moved by things, observe order and chaos,
The heart constantly guards against what has not yet occurred.
When the noble man attains his Way,
What is there to great peace!
○Same as above.
“Four Songs in the Shāng Mode”
The ruler sings in the gōng mode,
Broad and great, with wise plans.
The ministers respond in the shāng mode,
Hearing righteousness, then it can be practiced.
Yǒuxióng conducted governance,
Sought the Way from Róngchéng.
Yīn Tāng received the mandate,
Entrusted responsibility to Āhéng.
Loyal in his reverent service,
If guilty, he did not evade punishment.
Reciting his admonitions and remonstrances,
In speech, there was no hidden feeling.
Having firmness and decisiveness,
The four directions can be at peace.
Already praised, already elegant,
Under heaven then ascends to peace.
Focusing essence with single-mindedness,
Metal and stone are thereby opened.
If two minds are stirred,
Wife and children’s affection turns awry.
If it benefits the altars of soil and grain,
There is none who does not exhaust his heart.
Vast Heaven bestows blessings,
The sovereign’s head is only hale and hearty!

From *Collection of Music Bureau Poems*, scroll fifteen.
From *Records of Poetry*, scroll one hundred nineteen.
All rivers converge,
Thus the great sea is deep.
All talents gathered,
Therefore they can form the Dèng Forest.
A fierce tiger in the mountains,
No beast dares to encroach.
Loyal ministers in the state,
Under heaven there are no divergent hearts.
In the past, our cultured ancestor,
Held his heart and was vigilant in concern,
Drove and cut down jackals and wolves,
Managed and built this heavenly pace.
Now I have received the mandate,
And again dare not be idle or complacent.
Only you, my assistants in harmony,
Each should know vigilance and fear.
○Same as above.
Ritual and music already rectified,
Spirits and men are thereby harmonious.
Jades and silks have their order,
The will desires to still shield and spear.
Each shares in auspicious signs,
All swear to divide mountains and rivers.
Today we rejoice together,
Facing wine, we should sing.
The Way and virtue to be made clear,
Listen to the sound of striking bells.
Spiritual malevolence not to be equaled,
Observe the form of the cast tripod.
Fēng Palace having been courted,
The feudal lords then were reverent.
Qíyáng perhaps on a hunt,
Huáiyí from this were pacified.
If crossing a great river,
One speaks of relying on boat and oar.
As in harmonizing the tripod’s contents,
There is reliance on salt and plum.
Ruler and ministers as one body,
Can thereby still the dusty air.
Gaining men, then there is order;
What age lacks extraordinary talent?
○Same as above.
The force of wind is thus raised,
And the steps of the terrace are ordered in peace.
Zhònglí having ascended,
And heaven and earth’s positions are established.
Merit none can yield to,
Inscribed on the banners of the Grand Chamberlain.
The age does not lose its duties,
Receiving the covenant of red-haired victims.
Gathering tokens, distributing tokens,
Solemn and majestic at Yáo’s gate.
Only shields, only screens,
Lush and abundant in Zhōu’s plain.
Merit achieved and order settled,
Ritual and music thereby endure.
Restoring the son and making clear the rule,
What words had Jī Dàn?
○Same as above.
“Two Songs in the Jué Mode”
Ceasing weapons is seen in the wild where reins are cut,
Declaring campaigns is heard in the expedition to Dānshuǐ.
Trust and righteousness both preserved,
Then first forget food;
The five materials used together,
Who can do away with arms?
Although the sage’s great treasure is called position,
Truly heaven and earth’s great virtue is called life.
Jīng and Wèi flow together,
Clear and turbid differ in capacity;
Qín and sè played together,
Elegant and vulgar differ in sound.
Tumultuous masses of people,
Sound and teaching not uniform;
Vast and boundless traces of Yǔ,
Chariot tracks not yet united.
Aim encompassing the four seas,
Yet still reverent and frugal;
Heart embracing the cosmos,
Yet without arrogance or pride.
Words without pattern,
Cannot travel far;
Righteousness without establishment,
Diligence then achieves nothing.
Compassionate his heart,
Instruct with kindness and beneficence;
Flowing leniency for his faults,
Pity and compassion in canonical punishments.
○From *The Collected Works of Yǔ Zǐshān*, scroll seven.
From *Collection of Music Bureau Poems*, scroll fifteen.
From *Records of Poetry*, scroll one hundred nineteen.
Men of assistance and support,
Some come from fishing and angling;
Talents of cloud and rain,
Suddenly sigh in secluded valleys.
Seekers of fragrance pursue orchids in deep paths,
Discerners of rhythm probe bamboo in remote mountains.
Able to make his virtue bright,
Offered with the three affairs;
Establishing his wind and reputation,
Spoken of among the nine regions.
Harmoniously using the five regulations,
The wind is compliant in service;
Agriculturally using the eight policies,
Sweetness makes its grain.
Different winds share the same track,
Seen in the “Zhōu Nán”;
Different stalks bear the same ear,
Heard of from Táng Shū.
Severe cold and summer rain,
There is no mutual complaint;
Heaven covers, clouds spread,
Moistening, they seep and drip.
Fortunately, do not decline the simple men of high antiquity,
Almost can be sealed within neighboring houses.
○Same as above.
“Six Songs in the Zhǐ Mode”
Heaven and earth, by nurturing, cover and support;
Sun and moon, by constancy and brightness, shine upon.
The enlightened person takes the four seas as his task,
The wise ruler takes the hundred surnames as his heart.
Where water has waves and ripples, its source must be distant;
Where trees are spreading and lush, their roots must be deep.
Cloud and rain take to bestowing, none not reaching;
The court and temple seek talent, many are employed.
○From *The Collected Works of Yǔ Zǐshān*, scroll seven.
From *Collection of Music Bureau Poems*, scroll fifteen.
From *Records of Poetry*, scroll one hundred nineteen.
Pure winds spread governance, ever free from desire,
The ultimate Way guards men, able to transform customs.
Seeking benevolence and righteousness more urgently than water and fire,
Using ritual and deference more abundantly than beans and grains.
The Qūyì plant has no flatterers to point at,
The Xièzhì beast has no excessive punishments to gore.
The Kingly Way is vast and broad, employing non-action,
Under heaven, the four peoples—who could lack sufficiency!
○Same as above.
A sage is born once in a thousand years,
The Yellow River clears once in a thousand years.
Shètí follows this in marking the cycles,
The jade candles thus shine with brilliance.
The southeast can mend the earth’s gaps,
The northwest can rectify heaven’s tilt.
Riding giant turtles, the Eastern Sea can be crossed,
Wielding spades, the Southern Mountains can be leveled.
All immortals gather in audience at the Yáoshǔi,
The myriad emperors receive offerings in the bright court.
Harmony within, then fur drums and ren pipes play together,
Merits achieved, then bells and tripods are both inscribed.
○Same as above.
The three lights mark things and manifest forms,
The four seasons regulate and establish proper positions.
Thunder and wind amplify the echoes of mountains and peaks,
Cold and heat circulate the energies of yīn and yáng.
Martial achievements unify the six directions,
Civilizing teachings weave the warp and weft of the two realms.
Where the Way prevails, all are bathed in its virtue,
Where life is cherished, each multiplies its kind.
The white sun traverses the sky’s center and then shifts,
The bright moon spans the Milky Way, full and then wanes.
Able to wane and wane, already non-action,
Though full and full, yet not imperiled.
Open trust and righteousness as parks and gardens,
Establish morality and virtue as walls and moats.
The Zhōu dynasty examined the two prior eras’ additions and subtractions,
How rich and refined its culture can be known!
Páoxī personally attended to hunting and fishing,
Shénnóng personally grasped plowing and sowing.
Tāng then rescued from drought with toil and concern,
Yǔ then corrected caps without leisure.
Grass bends wherever the wind blows,
The gentleman’s people know they can be transformed.
Wishing to compare virtue to the Three Sovereigns,
Never once pursuing the tracks of the Five Hegemons.
○Same as above.
Slender threads unbroken form the grove’s thickness,
Tiny streams unceasing give birth to rivers.
In affairs, a hair’s breadth cannot be called light,
Considering far, guarding against the subtle, then no collapse.
Cloud officials are the great ruler who rules with folded hands,
The phoenix calendar belongs solely to the reverent and enlightened sovereign.
Sacrificing to the Supreme Deity and honoring the six ancestral temples,
Gazing at mountains and rivers and receiving homage from all lords.
The earth’s mirror opens up mountains and marshes together,
The River Chart shows fish and dragons jointly bearing it.
My net of heaven leaves nothing uncovered,
The nine gates of Chānghé, heaven’s gate, open.
Ministers and chancellors are mysteriously moved like wind and clouds,
Aiding and supporting, stars and constellations descend.
Already reviving the three sages of the Zhōu house,
Then raising the eight talents of the Táng dynasty.
The Shēn minister advises the left chancellor,
Tiānlǎo instructs governance in the central court.
It is fitting to take the wise as models,
Thus never elevating trust in treacherous ones.
○Same as above.
The true yáng’s harmonious energy makes all beings flourish,
The sovereign’s Way aligns, heaven and earth are honored.
The common people plow and plant in the garden of righteousness,
Gentlemen soar and glide in the park of ritual.
Those who gather its fruits think of its tree,
Those who drink its flow cherish its source.
Gāoyáo plans, and unrighteousness stays far,
Shìhuì governs, and all bandits flee.
Broad kindness makes even insects turn inward,
Manifest trust makes distant customs settle hearts.
On floating bridges, Yuèzhī people embrace horses,
In the royal park, Wūsūn people learn the qín.
Red jade is sent as tribute from the southern sea,
White rings are offered as treasures from the western hills.
No need to force openings into Dàxià,
No need to await broken horns at Dàilín.
○Same as above.
〈Five Songs in Yǔ Mode〉
Establishing a ruler is to shepherd the people,
Setting up laws is to quell disorder.
The chief villain was already in Náncháo,
The arch-fiend then fled north.
Dwelling in auspicious energy that fills the four directions,
In radiance and splendor, two dawns appear.
Thus rain bestows as in “Jiě,”
Thus wind blows as in “Huàn.”
The Zhōu’s Wén and Wǔ’s great foundation,
Shining upon all under heaven with cultural thought.
A thousand years, all sages flourish brightly,
Seven hundred years, in me the destined time.
Truly, vast heaven has its ordained mandate,
May all four quarters be instructed by it.

When times are stable, draw close to kin’s customs,
When times are chaotic, first distance from the ambitious.
Cross the Guìlín forests and drive elephants,
Cross the Ruòshuǐ river and receive swans.
Already floating the breath of a thousand lǚ pipes,
Still blowing the winds of the eight pitch-standards.
Coins in the treasury rot on strings,
Granaries like Chángpíng overflow with red grains.
In the fire star’s position, now cold now hot,
Yearly harmony, one wind one rain.
Hearing bells and chimes,
Think of borderlands;
Hearing shēng and yú pipes,
Think of stored provisions.
Yáokūn jade and xiǎodàng bamboo are already submitted,
Strange stones, lead, and pine are arranged in order.
Chánglè’s fine horses fill the stables,
Shuǐhéng’s gold becomes the treasury.
○Same as above.
All rivers revere the great sea,
All stars look up to the North Star.
The nine provinces are unified by Yǔ’s traces,
The four seas combine virtue as Yáo’s ministers.
The morning sun perches on the singing phoenix,
The sacred grounds pasture the bānlín beast.
Clouds like jade leaves in five colors,
Moon with golden waves and two wheels.
Cool winds welcome the season’s northern hunt,
Minor heat warns of the southern tour.
Mountains hide no purple jade,
Earth hoards no yellow silver.
Though campaigning south, yet northern complaints,
Truly conquering west, yet eastern guests.
Already eternally purified across the four seas,
Finally there is celebration for the one man.
○Same as above.
Setting pitch with Línglíng’s jade tubes,
Tuning bells with Shǐpíng’s bronze ruler.
Below Lóngmén, the solitary tóng tree,
By the Sìshuǐ’s banks, the sounding stone.
The river spirit thus yields jade tablets,
The mountain essence therefore offers jade discs.
Cleansing the nine rivers and levying taxes,
Ascending the Sānwēi mountains and receiving tributes.
Northern village’s grain with six ears,
Jiānghuái’s thatch with three ridges.
Fit for jade cases to seal the fēng and shàn sacrifices,
Fit for golden cords to examine the registers.
Eternally preserving the great name,
Enough to spread glory in the records.
○Same as above.
The highest is to establish virtue,
The next is called establishing words.
Cultivating goodness thrives in attending to roots,
Eradicating evil exhausts in blocking sources.
Profound and deep, its wisdom is then rich,
Bright and clear, its Way is then honored.
The wealth of benevolence and righteousness never lacks,
The ritual of loyalty and trust is not excessive.
Moving heaven, none it does not reach,
Only the times, no darkness it does not penetrate.
Practicing virtue, the heart rests and days are blessed,
Practicing deceit, the heart toils and days are clumsy.
Unless by firmness overcoming and covering righteousness,
There is no escape from eradication.
○Same as above.
〈Memorial Congratulating the Pacification of Yè Capital〉
〈Memorial Congratulating the Pacification of Yè Capital〉
Your subject, [name], states:
Your subject has heard that since Tàishān and Liángfǔ,
There have already been seventy-two dynasties;
After the dragon chart and turtle script,
Again over three thousand years have passed.
Though again establishing laws and setting up offices,
Rituals differ and music varies,
Yet down to patterned shields and martial arrays,
Sharpening wood and stringing bows,
The heart to roll up the world like a mat,
The ambition to encompass the eight wildernesses,
The principle is one and the same.
I humbly consider that Your Majesty the Emperor,
grasping the pivot of heaven,
holding the axis of earth,
drives the winds and clouds,
and commands the dragons and tigers.
With profound and resolute inner judgment,
You need not labor for counsel from Lìmù;
with celestial-strategy courage and decisiveness,
You have no need to inquire of Róngchéng.
Thus, where Your awe-inspiring might shakes,
it is like a great fire meeting goose down;
where Your banners and drums approach,
it is like a gale sweeping autumn leaves.
I have privately heard that the Róng and Yí tribes of Yī and Luò,
and the usurping pretenders of Yōu and Bìng,
bearing maps and records,
have already returned to the Chancellor's office;
those holding jade seals and silk ribbons,
all proceed to the camp of the central army.
A century of fugitives from punishment,
have thus been driven to the end of their lairs;
enemy grudges of three dynasties,
were suddenly swept clean.
In the past, the campaign of the Zhou king at the Wěi River,
still required a second expedition;
the battle of Xuānyuán at Shànggǔ,
still needed nine assaults.
Never has there been a single morning's command,
a solitary divine consideration deciding all,
pacifying the entire realm,
and gloriously establishing rule over all under heaven.
Of the twenty-eight constellations,
only the single star of Wú and Yuè remains;
of the twelve hundred states,
only the small waters of Línzhōu are omitted.
As for the years of Xiánkāng,
when the four quarters first stabilized;
the era of Jiànwǔ,
when the feudal lords all came to court,
they cannot be spoken of in the same breath!
Even if the eight winds all sang together,
it would be insufficient to praise Your heroic fame;
even if the six musical forms were all performed,
there would be no way to sing of Your divine martial prowess.
Sitting at the fishing terrace to address the multitudes,
Sì Qǐ continued the achievements of Xià Yǔ;
entering the suburbs of Shāng to demand retribution,
Jī Fā fulfilled the aspirations of Zhōu Wén.
The unalterable Way,
is this not great filial piety!
Nowadays, the Lùtái has been dispersed,
the detached palaces have been dismissed,
weapons are stored in the armory,
horses are returned to Huàshān,
the system of the Bright Hall is established,
the music of "Great Martial" is performed,
how magnificent!
Heaven bestows blessings,
such as have never been before.
It is only proper to establish a commandant in the southeast,
stationed south of Bǐjǐng;
and a lookout in the northwest,
placed north of Jiāohé.
Then command the Eastern Sovereign,
announce to the azure heavens,
raise the altar and jade tablet,
with silver cords and jade cases,
declare the completion of Your achievements,
so as to have no cause for shame in virtue.
Your servant, undeservedly honored,
administers the eastern frontier,
unable to personally attend the court,
to witness the great celebration,
cannot contain his utmost joy and eager excitement.
Respectfully, I dispatch my Registrar and accompanying official Cáo Mǐn to present this memorial for Your attention.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 566.
Also briefly seen in *Yìwén Lèijù*, scroll 59.
"Memorial Congratulating on the New Music (Emperor Wu of Zhou)"
Your servants say:
We have heard that when heaven and earth move harmoniously,
then thunder emerges as a sign of ease;
when a sage achieves success,
then the wind's movement has its rhythm.
Thus, the six virtues reside in the office of "Xiánchí,"
and mountains and valleys can be harmonized;
the eight winds enter the performance of "Chéngyún,"
and humans and spirits do not intermingle.
Our great ancestor, Emperor Wén,
organized the state and regulated the countryside,
established offices and divided duties,
transformed Wèi to create Zhōu,
shifted customs and rectified elegance,
clothed in robes to receive myriad states in audience,
holding jade tablets to meet the feudal lords.
As for managing records and texts,
collating amidst smoke and ashes,
the Music Master lacked no chapter,
the Minister of Rites neglected no classic.
How could it be merely that the ten pieces of "Shāng Odes,"
were obtained from the Grand Master's chamber;
or the "Yú Documents" and five rites,
were taken from the palace of the Reverent King?
We humbly consider that Your Majesty, succeeding with martial virtue,
continuing the enterprise from Zhōngyáng,
applying the brightness of sun and moon,
stirring thoughts from deep springs.
The subtleties of pitch and calendar are made clear,
without troubling the Grand Historian;
the measurements of yin and yang,
personally determined by the Celestial Official.
Thus You are able to examine and harmonize the eight tones,
study meticulously the six dynasties,
enfief Jìn and Wèi as two kings,
arrange Yīn and Zhōu as the three honored lines.
Although vermilion shields and jade axes,
still recognize the classical models;
plain knee-covers and crimson robes,
still rely on powerful possession.
They are not like "Mountain Clouds" uniquely arising,
the eight trigrams taking form;
the phoenix flying,
the nine provinces observing virtue.
Altering the metal performance into eight rows,
combining the celestial origin in the six dances.
The sound contains stone chimes,
further entering the ascending songs;
the melody begins with the great bell,
again participating with jade pipes.
Sufficient to move heaven and earth and communicate with the spirits,
to make imperial virtue prosperous and illuminate the celestial signs.
In the past, dwelling in seclusion at Xuánhù,
the composition lay in "Yúnmén";
the army crossing Měngjīn,
the practice of dance returned to mountain stillness.
Thus it encompassed the three names,
harmonizing perfectly for an era.
The creator is called a sage,
is this not what heaven has opened?
How could it be merely the road drum and spirit drum,
the Kūsāng and Gūzhú trees,
vast and great,
magnificent and splendid.
This shows that the Filial and Incorrupt of Línglíng,
vainly transmitted jade pipes;
the Grand Administrator of Shǐpíng,
emptily praised bronze rulers.
We, your servants, have all partaken of the heavenly music,
together observed the performance,
the courtyard broad and spacious,
the railings offering distant views.
The lofty teeth stand majestic,
the fierce stands sturdy.
A verdant phoenix raises banners,
a divine alligator sets up drums.
Obscure clouds and mist,
swirl and surge over hills and mounds.
Sweet springs and sweet dew fly together,
red wild geese and dappled unicorns descend together.
If sent to Lǔ to request a viewing,
one would surely see its abundant virtue;
if going to Qí and forgetting flavor,
one would certainly know its perfection and beauty.
In the past, deep-water fish hearing the melody,
could still raise their scales;
stable horses hearing the strings,
could still lift their heads from the manger.
We, your servants, are truly ashamed of our musical understanding,
but dare not forget our delight!
If asked to detail its tones and rhythms,
that would be far beyond us;
we can only record its clanging resonance,
and in this consider ourselves fortunate.
We cannot contain our sincere joy and celebration.
Respectfully we approach the court hall,
to present this memorial for Your attention.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 569.
"Memorial Requesting Retirement on Behalf of General Yán"
"Memorial Requesting Retirement on Behalf of General Yán"
Your subject so-and-so states:
Your subject has heard the Book of Rites say:
"When a senior official reaches seventy, he retires from court,
hands over his household to his sons,
his meals are then served with double delicacies,
and his clothing matches the seasonal regulations."
Your subject, since entering service to devote himself to the state,
for over forty years,
has encountered changing fortunes,
rising from obscurity to prominence.
The Great Ancestor, Emperor Wén, rescued from peril and aided in distress,
and swiftly possessed the strategic passes and rivers.
Your subject truly had no talent,
yet served in a minor capacity.
From the turmoil at the Luòyáng feast,
to the banners and drums at Héliáng,
the white-horse troops at Huàyīn,
to the yellow-sand battle array at Héqū.
Although your subject exerted himself,
he could devise no extraordinary strategies.
His merit was meager, yet his rewards were generous;
he achieved things by relying on others.
The annual record of imperial favor
has always filled him with shame.
Then he encountered the Zhōu dynasty,
which rose to power through abdication and virtue,
and received the mandate with songs of praise.
As the sovereign became honored, his ministers were promoted,
and honors and favor were frequently bestowed.
The Three Dukes, through casting tripods and depicting creatures,
knew their divine craft;
the Five Ranks, with their jade tablets as auspicious ornaments,
guarded their palaces and chambers.
What virtue does your subject possess,
to have both of these?
Moreover, for the office of Water and Earth,
Wáng Liáng was summoned because he fulfilled a prophecy;
for the command of armies and weapons,
Hán Xìn was uniquely honored by ascending the altar to receive his appointment.
Speaking of such comparable figures,
what kind of person is your subject?
Now, the four seas are not yet at peace,
and three powers stand in tripartite confrontation.
This is the time when Your Majesty toils with concern,
and when all the lords should demonstrate their effectiveness.
Yet your subject's years are already many,
and old age has also arrived.
He cannot participate in the affairs of guests,
and wrongly occupies the ranks of the nobles.
Holding office without merit, eating the salary for nothing,
he has long disordered the constant statutes;
bearing burdens invites bandits,
merely troubling the officials.
Moreover, cold and heat have been contrary,
the regulation of his vitality has lost its order,
wind and dampness assail him together,
and his essence and vigor are already exhausted.
Even if, like Lián Pō, he forced himself to eat,
or like Mǎ Yuán, he mounted the saddle,
seeking to repay your grace,
how could he serve effectively?
The joy of Róng Qǐqī
is merely enough for self-contentment;
the words of Zhú Zhīwǔ
are beyond his capability.
He specially begs to be relieved of his official post,
and to speak of returning to his original garb.
This matter accords with the request for retirement of one's bones,
and is not a scheme to seek the gift of a stool and cane.
If your subject, like one moving his illness to the northern hills,
or returning to grow old on the eastern heights,
with his mountains, rivers, thatched altar, and fief,
returns them all to the Minister of Merits,
and his ducal or marquisate jade tablets,
are returned and sealed by the Keeper of the Auspicious Regalia,
then the court will have no one occupying a position presumptuously,
and your subject will avoid the blame of hindering the worthy.
The Yú clan's care for the aged—
how dare he hope for the glory of the Eastern Hall?
The Zhōu court, with its multitudes like white flowering reeds—
how could he expect the ceremony of the western suburbs?
Only, gazing up at the heavenly majesty,
now about to depart from being so close,
lingering before the palace gates,
in private his sorrow and attachment increase.
He cannot bear the feeling of knowing when to stop.
○ From Wényuàn Yīnghuá, scroll 603.
〈Memorial Submitting a Request for Retirement on Behalf of Another〉
Your subject Sù states:
Your subject has heard that when a leaf is about to fall,
does it wait for the wind and dew?
All rivers reach the sea,
but the stagnant pools dry up by themselves.
Your subject is moved by this,
to sorrow and to choke.
Your subject so-and-so respectfully expresses gratitude.
Your subject, since the end of mid-spring,
has found his old ailment gradually worsening.
His two feet are quite lame,
his four limbs are not agile.
When supported to walk, he stumbles like the man from Hándān;
straining to see, he lacks the clarity of Lílóu.
How could he lead in these remaining duties,
and muddle these constant statutes?
Your Majesty's grace is all-encompassing and accommodating,
and you have been unwilling to cast him aside.
But your humble subject's distress has reached an extreme,
and he is increasingly unable to bear it.
This is why your subject blames and grieves for himself,
his tears followed by blood.
Your subject so-and-so respectfully expresses gratitude.
Your subject specially inherited his ancestors' legacy,
his advancement not due to others.
Your Majesty, pitying your subject's uselessness,
promoted an upright man, though he is blunt.
Since receiving the charts at Tàijí Hall,
and proclaiming edicts in the Central Secretariat,
Your Majesty has embraced your subject with single-hearted trust,
and entrusted your subject with sole authority.
For nine years he hoped to ascend to the council of ministers;
for eight years he has served as Minister of Rites.
Going out, he commanded regiments with banners;
entering, he participated in the impartial mirror of judgment.
Sometimes, atop the Cloud Terrace,
your humble subject was included in consultations for advice;
sometimes, below the Sun-Viewing Peak,
he was commanded to draft texts for engraving on stone.
Beautiful and fluent—
your subject is indeed especially ashamed.
He dared not bear the slightest violation of the clear laws,
yet his contribution to the profound creation was as slight as a drop.
The sun and moon steal away; ice and charcoal,
mingle in his sincere heart.
He recalls that previously, accompanying government affairs,
personally receiving virtuous instructions,
Your Majesty said to your subject and others, who had long attended at the palace steps,
that their descendants would still receive continued protection.
Your subject, an ant,
suddenly bore a mountain.
Your subject should, in life, exhaust his strength,
and in death, still exert his effort.
Secretly, he did not know his end,
and did not know when to stop.
Among the court officials, three or several,
who were your subject's peers,
your subject, not yet sixty,
compared to them, is young.
Yet your subject alone increasingly suffers decline,
his illness not waiting for years.
A full measure reaches its limit;
fullness invites loss.
Passing time often contradicts the hope of recovery without medicine;
all day long he is still tied to the clinging mulberry.
Seeing that this outcome is inevitable,
he is wary of clinging to glory.
He humbly begs that his current post be removed,
to retire and complete his remaining years.
Observe that your subject's glory cannot be sustained;
pity that his allotted strength cannot be forced.
This would be your subject's fortune.
How could he have realized that at the gate of Rénshòu Hall,
there would be this one audience;
and at the lodgings of Chéngmíng Gate,
there would be no chance to pay respects again?
His spirit and energy are already exhausted,
and with each moment his sorrow increases.
To receive your sagely discernment places him ahead of many scholars;
to be distant from your sacred countenance—how far is a petty official?
He only hopes that when the three roads are opened,
and the myriad chariots patrol the capital,
pleasing the multitudes of the western region who long for you,
he may reach those who follow the east wind.
If his endangered soul might linger,
and his dried bones seem to remain,
this would be your subject's contentment,
not what he presumes to hope for.
Your subject has also heard:
For driving and performing service,
one first discards the worn-out nag;
for soaring and gathering to celebrate success,
one recently discards the bird with broken wings.
They still know their twilight,
how much more does your subject!
Hearing this, he has not dared to delay his request;
this is your subject's earnest attachment.
As for neglecting his office,
your subject deserves to have his offense recorded.
He cannot bear the extreme of trembling fear and clinging attachment.
○ From Wényuàn Yīnghuá, scroll 603.
〈Memorial of the Prince of Qí Presenting a White Rabbit〉
〈Memorial of the Prince of Qí Presenting a White Rabbit〉
I have heard that when the imperial domain seeks to expand far and wide,
the jade tiger roars at dawn;
when chariot tracks first open,
the silver deer comes to pay tribute.
I humbly consider that Your Majesty, brilliant and enlightened above,
reverently occupies the honored position,
your virtue moves the heavenly gates,
your might shifts the earth's axis.
Thus winds and mists shine brightly,
feathers and fur bring auspicious signs,
the historians never cease recording,
the storehouses are never empty for a day.
I, having received the command as chief commander,
use it to pacify the border regions,
wherever my headquarters reach,
first arriving at Xióng Shān,
the vanguard, anticipating no concerns,
captured a white hare.
Its radiance surpasses the Yuè pheasant,
its beauty outshines the Qín fox.
The virtue of the moon matches the omen,
the essence of metal manifests as an auspicious sign.
Presenting this auspiciousness to the imperial carriage and eulogies,
its efficacy differs from unrolled maps,
the traces of reverence are already clear,
the opportunity to respond to affairs thus emerges.
My humble journey,
truly follows the strategy of Shǎn,
the auspicious sign with its pure quality,
greatly enhances the western aura.
I hope to repeatedly receive the temple's calculations,
and proceed to display majesty,
subduing Dài and pacifying Qí,
dividing Hán and splitting Zhào.
I cannot contain the feelings of joy and eagerness.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá* 612.
Also briefly seen in *Yìwén Lèijù* 95.
〈Memorial of Prince Qí Presenting a Gray Crow〉
〈Memorial of Prince Qí Presenting a Gray Crow〉
Your subject so-and-so states:
I have heard that the pheasant flying in Nányáng
still elucidated the hegemonic plan;
the crane descending at Jiànzhāng
still harmonized the vital energy.
How much more when the Yú court announces an auspicious sign,
the Jī altar presents a propitious omen,
all highly value the heart that knows feeding,
truly prize the nature capable of understanding.
I humbly consider that His Majesty the Emperor,
instructs the people with virtue,
governs the four seas with filial piety,
the Shetí star follows the order,
the world is cultured and enlightened.
Thus the eastern sea sends forth fowl,
suddenly changing their black quality;
the western mountain conveys feathers,
some transform into gray essence.
On the thirtieth day of last month,
traveling to Shǎn Zhōu,
I obtained the report of Grand Governor Mò Rén Huílèliè,
who stated that in the archery hall of the prefecture,
he saw a gray crow,
circling and soaring among the trees and thickets,
circling without leaving,
halting the essence of the riding wood,
turning the wings that govern the wind.
I immediately summoned Commandant so-and-so and others,
to witness it together.
This truly results from the extension of ritual reverence,
the response to filial compassion,
it is fitting to return the auspicious sign to the secret charts,
record the propitious omen in the imperial registers,
to glorify the utmost virtue,
and achieve the effect of peace and prosperity.
Do not let the red phoenix linger,
solely performing the song of buried jade;
nor the black crane hover,
uniquely excelling in the dance of holding pearls.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá* 612.
〈Memorial of Prince Qí Presenting a Red Sparrow〉
〈Memorial of Prince Qí Presenting a Red Sparrow〉
Your subject so-and-so states:
I have heard that the pheasant flying in Nányáng
is still discussed regarding Qín's hegemony;
the crane descending at Jiànzhāng
still illuminates Hàn's virtue.
Now Heaven does not begrudge treasures,
Earth must present auspicious signs,
naturally there should be tallies at Chánglè Palace,
and Wénchāng inaugurates propitious omens.
I humbly consider that the Emperor,
reverent, enlightened, cultured, and thoughtful,
only through toil accomplishes affairs.
Observing the movements of the sun and moon,
he truly regulates all officials.
The sea waters are without waves,
the heavenly stars do not move.
On the thirteenth day of the fourth month last,
I received a dispatch from Lǒngyòu Commandery Administrator Lǐ Huī stating:
in Wéngǔ Forest, Bóyáng County, Qīngshuǐ Commandery, Qínchuān, within a household, a red sparrow was captured,
its radiance equal to the vermilion phoenix,
its color resembling the crimson crow.
Descending fire and flying essence,
as if entering the office of the ducal carriage;
flowing gold forming a vessel,
as if ascending the Língyún Terrace.
Carefully considering that the red sparrow holding a document,
rested at the door of Fēng,
Zhōu's receiving of the mandate,
arose from this auspicious sign.
Observing the present event,
it matches the tally and agrees with the covenant.
Truly it can be depicted in the auspicious registers,
recorded in eulogies among the Confucian scholars,
the event suffices to complete the terrace,
the name worthy of recording the title.
How could it merely be that the Governor of Yúnzhōng
sees the red heart serving the ruler;
or the Pénglái youth
knows the white jade ring repaying kindness?
We, your subjects, witnessing the auspicious response in advance,
our feelings are urgent with constant celebration,
we cannot contain the utmost joy.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá* 612.
〈Memorial on Behalf of the Duke of Jìnyáng Presenting Jade Pitch-Pipes, Steelyard, Ruler, Dou, and Shēng〉
〈Memorial on Behalf of the Duke of Jìnyáng Presenting Jade Pitch-Pipes, Steelyard, Ruler, Dou, and Shēng〉
Your subject so-and-so states:
I have heard that since the Three Powers were established,
the way of ruler and minister has been set forth;
when the Six Positions were timely completed,
the achievements of rites and music were thus rectified.
Therefore, they harmonize with the sun and moon,
measure yīn and yáng,
delight the myriad people,
and serve as models for the ten thousand states.
I humbly consider that the Emperor,
responding to the tally, drives Heaven,
unfolds the charts and receives the mandate,
relies on the Great Sun and suspends the images,
treads Wénchāng and establishes the standard,
the white jade ring manifests the sign of yielding virtue,
the dark jade tablet announces the auspiciousness of accomplished success,
the Grand Steps are already level,
the ascent to the center can be practiced,
surely then the waters will establish a thousand years,
the mountains will proclaim ten thousand ages.
I humbly observe the imperial edict,
correcting the musical pitches,
deliberating on the celestial phenomena.
Playing the Huángzhōng and singing the Dàlǚ,
transforming the Gūzhú and dancing the Yúnmén,
all instruments are chosen for their clarity and openness,
sounds follow peace and joy.
The four divisions are already clear,
the three subtleties are also settled.
Thus hearing the bell at Luòpǔ,
one immediately discerns discordant sounds;
listening to the bell at Hándān,
one first knows the resonance and rhyme.
The two equinoxes and two solstices,
are carried out by the officials of the calendar;
the nine transformations and nine completions,
are entrusted to the office of harmony.
Sufficient to move Heaven and Earth,
affect spirits and deities,
influence customs, and balance cold and heat.
How could it merely be chanting in stream valleys,
or phoenixes soaring back and forth?
Thus we know that before the temple at Línglíng,
one only seeks Shùn's pipes;
below the city of Shǐpíng,
one emptily discusses Zhōu's ruler.
I have heard that the sovereign establishes the rites,
and the subjects practice the ceremonies;
the ruler sets the laws,
and the ministers carry out the affairs.
I have respectfully crafted a set of jade pitch-pipes,
along with jade scales, rulers, pecks, pints, and measures,
and have only now achieved completion.
As for dividing grains and accumulating millets,
measuring silk threads and counting bamboo tubes,
I truly rely on receiving the sagely regulations,
and consulting the divine thoughts.
What I hope is that the seasonal changes shift the yin pipes,
without toiling the ashes from Hénèi;
the qi moves the yang bells,
without awaiting the bamboo from Jīnmén.
Yet my jade work is trivial,
and my craftsmanship shallow,
insufficient to display in the Imperial Academy,
or add luster to the measures.
I present the instruments with this memorial for your attention.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 613.
Also seen in *Yìwén Lèijù*, scroll 5,
with deletions.
〈Memorial Presenting the "Rhapsody on the *Xiàngjīng*"〉
Your subject so-and-so states:
I have humbly studied the imperial composition *Xiàngjīng*,
and observed the elephant game,
my heart leaping with joy,
unable to contain my dancing.
I consider that nature and the Way of Heaven,
are fundamentally beyond seeking,
yet directly as if suspended like the sun and moon,
I have thus been able to gaze upon them.
The Nine Provinces already settled,
I closely face the *Hétú*;
the four chariot tracks aligned with the plumb line,
I fully observe the jade tablets.
Before the black crane flies,
I first hear the sound of metal and stone;
without ascending Chìchéng,
I alone see the aura of mist and clouds.
Setting a tube to measure,
the light and shadow grow higher;
sinking jade to observe,
the deep springs appear farther.
Unaware of my limits,
I composed a rhapsody from emptiness,
the words lacking brilliance,
the learning without polish.
Thus I dare to present it,
truly feeling deeply ashamed.
Moreover, the distance of the sun,
was originally not a question for a child;
the encompassing canopy of heaven,
how could it be a topic for a mere scholar?
I presume to present this for your attention,
humbly increasing my sweat of shame to the utmost.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 610.
〈Memorial Congratulating on the Abdication to the Crown Prince〉
〈Memorial Congratulating on the Abdication to the Crown Prince〉
Your subject so-and-so states:
I have humbly seen the edict of the nineteenth day of the second month,
abdicating the throne to the Crown Prince.
In ancient times, descending to dwell at Ruòshuǐ,
elevation to office had distinctions of superiority and inferiority;
coming to court at Yuèyáng,
succession had differences between ruler and subject.
They cannot compare with the two suns in heaven,
the sun at double noon,
shining together in splendor,
doubly bright and doubly illuminating,
spoken of in the same breath!
I consider that the Celestial Origin Emperor,
a sage creating sages,
honoring kin by honoring kin,
condescending to yield to the capable,
humbly relinquishing the sacred vessel.
Wishing to have all officials in harmony,
first hearing the custom of yielding;
the world in non-action,
early recognizing the son of our ruler.
Therefore, employing uniquely perceptive wisdom,
performing extraordinary deeds,
not contravening Heaven's timing,
but following and upholding it.
The Crown Prince, personally upholding myriad states,
his Way illuminating the four gates,
long bearing the tally of repeated mandate,
truly accords with the Heaven-founded destiny,
unrelated to restoring the son and clarifying the ruler,
different from transferring from Yú to serving Xià.
Whether diminished or augmented,
there may still be two heavens;
as Lí or as Huǒ,
what hinders two suns?
Moreover, Píngyáng and Púbǎn,
had worthy ministers numbering twenty-five;
Zhuānxū and Gāoxīn,
had talented sons from sixteen clans.
With such planning affairs,
how could there be no success!
Drumming vigorously,
dancing gracefully.
Naturally, the eight winds will circulate,
auspicious clouds gather,
the Five Elders roam together,
the Three Stars move in radiance.
How could it merely be double dragons bestowed again,
nine pheasants flying once more!
The Emperor, remote as Gūshè,
rightly should ride clouds and drive dragons,
inquire about the Way at Kōngtóng,
how could he again be like leaves falling before autumn?
I, your subject, was born in the age of Yáo,
encountering the days of Shùn,
witnessing the celebration of renewal,
truly feel emotions ten thousand times the norm.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 557.
Also briefly seen in *Yìwén Lèijù*, scroll 16.
〈Memorial Declining the Post of Imperial Preceptor and General of Agile Cavalry for the Duke of Qǐ〉
〈Memorial Declining the Post of Imperial Preceptor and General of Agile Cavalry for the Duke of Qǐ〉
Your subject so-and-so states:
I have humbly seen the imperial edict,
appointing me as Commissioner with Extraordinary Powers, General of Agile Cavalry, Excellency with Authority Equal to the Three Ministers, and Imperial Preceptor of the Palace.
Receiving the imperial words,
my heart and soul tremble in awe.
I have heard that Yáo divided the four peaks,
thereby ordering the sacrifices to mountains and rivers;
Shùn appointed the nine ministers,
thereby making the sun and moon shine with glory.
One must model virtue,
clearly test through merit,
only then can harmony be achieved with myriad states,
and all achievements be splendid.
I, your subject, lacked learning in youth,
and in maturity lacked cultivation,
at the gate of Hóngdū,
unable to determine its chapters and sentences;
at the frontier of Jīlù,
unable to inscribe its steles and tablets.
Relying on the tributary streams of the celestial river,
attaching to the branching limbs of the Ruòmù tree,
at Dōngyuè I have a name for morning lodging,
at the Southern Palace my name is recorded at the gates,
yet in my mediocrity and inferiority,
I have long known my fullness and excess.
Wǔyáng, by virtue of being a meritorious minister,
was specially appointed Imperial Preceptor;
Dōngpíng, by virtue of being a maternal younger brother of honor,
was elevated to supreme general.
What virtue do I possess,
to combine such honors?
I lost the shade of my family courtyard early,
before I could even lean against the wall,
my mother's kind instruction,
compassionate and toilsome,
just as I reached adulthood,
was again faced with abandonment.
The memorial table as if present,
how can I bear to leave the nurturing grace?
Unrequited unto heaven's end,
knocking my head on the ground, the burden is hard to bear.
I wish to remain in the grassy mounds and hills,
lifelong in the burial grounds,
with frost and dew expressing seasonal feelings,
swallows and sparrows displaying circling hearts.
Never expecting the heavenly favor to pour forth so abundantly,
mistakenly elevating and selecting me.
Now, with the jade candle harmoniously regulated,
it is not an age of metal and leather;
with the jade sphere governing orderly,
how could one forget the remnants of pines and catalpas?
Moreover, a single bent branch,
will ultimately endanger a nine-tiered tower;
a puddle from a horse's hoof,
will surely injure a carriage traveling a thousand miles.
The Emperor, with profound wisdom and enlightened thought,
radiates his virtue across the realm.
Ritual norms extend to the four directions,
so none should dare to deprive this subject of his resolve;
governing the world through filial piety,
it is only natural to sympathize with this subject’s sentiments.
The Great Ancestor served as a teacher,
yet still sought states of the same lineage;
the chief commander rides in the imperial carriage,
but another capable and worthy minister is selected.
I humbly hope that upon reading this memorial on the green rush mat,
Your Majesty will graciously grant this sincere plea;
issuing an edict from the Phoenix Pond,
specially accept this earnest summons.
Then Heaven’s compassion will not be excessive,
my private wish will be fulfilled,
and this subject’s place of refuge
will indeed be secured.
Unable to contain my anxiety and trembling sincerity,
I reverently approach the court hall,
presenting this memorial for Your Majesty’s attention.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 578.
“Memorial Requesting Hereditary Enfeoffment for Descendants of Meritorious Officials Who Died in Royal Service”
“Memorial Requesting Hereditary Enfeoffment for Descendants of Meritorious Officials Who Died in Royal Service”
I have heard that those who govern the people by law
must have their sacrifices recorded in the ritual codes;
those who stabilize the state through their labors
must have heirs to continue their lineage.
Sūnshū Áo’s sacrifices were not recorded,
which harmed the reputation of a good minister;
Nǚshū Qí’s descendants were cut off,
truly diminishing the standing of a worthy official.
Carefully examining the regulations of the sixteenth year of the Dàtǒng era,
it states that those who previously held noble titles and died in royal service without heirs
may have collateral sons inherit their titles,
but those who did not die in royal service
are not permitted to inherit according to previous records.
The meritorious officials of the five ranks
all toiled diligently for the royal house,
personally faced hardships,
warded off disasters,
and assisted in great plans.
If they fell ill one day
and passed away,
unfortunately leaving no descendants,
their sacrifices would cease entirely,
which is insufficient according to ritual
and damaging according to righteousness.
Before requesting a hunt in the Shanglin Park,
their marquisates were already revoked;
before donning the chānyú robes,
their fiefdoms were first removed.
I humbly consider that the Emperor honors virtue and rewards merit,
reviving the fallen and continuing the severed.
Hearing the war drums, he thinks of his generals;
viewing the Cloud Terrace, he remembers his old ministers.
How can there be those whose merits preserved the altars of state
yet have no descendants to uphold them?
Those who served with utmost loyalty
yet have no shrine for sacrifices?
The Zhou dynasty made covenants with its feudal lords,
based on their worldly achievements;
the Han dynasty swore oaths over mountains and rivers,
with righteousness enduring long.
I have heard that preserving someone’s state
is greater than rescuing them from disaster;
establishing someone’s heir
is more important than building their tomb.
I privately consider that in the Yin dynasty, succession continued
without neglecting the minor lineages;
the rise and fall of the Zhou house
valued the preservation of posterity.
Those who succeeded Gāomì for generations,
were they solely the direct descendants of Dèng Yǔ?
Those who inherited Píngyáng over successive reigns,
must they necessarily be the direct grandsons of Cáo Cān?
I humbly believe that if one served with merit in life,
even if not dying in royal service,
though from collateral lines,
they should all be permitted to inherit.
Thus may the spirit of Bó Yǒu
not become a malevolent ghost;
the ghosts of Ruò Áo
may not go hungry.
The hidden and manifest respond in praise,
and humans and spirits are but a step apart.
○From *Yìwén Lèijù*, scroll 51.
“Letter of Thanks for the Preface to the *Collection of Prince Téng*”
Your humble servant states:
I have respectfully read the decree,
bestowing upon me the preface to the collection.
Like the Purple Palace shining from afar,
it transmits the teachings of Quèlǐ;
like the Blue Bird flying from a distance,
it delivers the jade of layered walls.
As for the jade trees in the Gānquán Palace,
a grove of them,
or the six-inch pearls before the Xuánwǔ Gate,
they cannot compare to this radiance,
nor match this illuminating brilliance.
Measured and balanced,
it harmonizes the eight winds;
rising ever higher in melody,
it nearly reaches three feet from heaven.
Your Highness’s heroic talent surpasses the age,
your untrammeled spirit spans the clouds,
a Yán Yuān from Jìběi,
a Confucius from west of the Pass.
Comparing your brushwork,
it is like wind and rain vying in flight;
discussing your literary elegance,
it transforms like fish and dragons in a hundred ways.
Grapevines winding around the halls,
newly opening the Jiéshí Palace;
tall bamboos lining the ponds,
first creating the Suīyáng Garden.
Glazed cups floating wine,
parrots bearing goblets.
Songs from the Phoenix Grotto,
dance tunes from the鸾Forest.
Moreover, drifting clouds follow the rain,
swirling snow accompanies the wind.
The commandant of Húyáng
already became a cause for joy;
the marquis of Chōnglíng
was indeed a place to dispel sorrow.
I have always lacked talent,
with few compositions to my name.
Moreover, during the Jiànyè calamities,
I barely escaped the scholar’s execution ground;
in the Jiānglíng disasters,
I nearly followed the scholars to the grave.
As for my scattered manuscripts and lost scrolls,
they all fell into the dust;
red-rolled and blue-boxed texts,
mostly turned to ashes.
In recent years, prolonged illness has lingered,
time passes while I barely watch and breathe,
the sunset of life approaches,
the willow weakens with age,
not without the sorrow of autumn’s aura,
truly harboring the regret of a road’s end.
Thus my spirit is confused and disordered,
much like Sòng Yù;
my speech stammers and halts,
even worse than Yáng Xióng.
With each chant and each verse,
this becomes evident.
Those seeking amusement do not ask for me,
those who understand music do not employ me.
Not having Bān Chāo’s ambition,
I long ago abandoned my brush;
not seeing Lù Jī’s writings,
I long equated my inkstone with burning.
As for what remains after decay,
the fragments left behind,
they have already been mixed into patched robes,
or used at times to cover sauce jars.
Your sagely compassion took pity,
and thus deigned to preserve and record them.
Only now do I realize that excessive praise
leads a gentleman to misspeak;
reckless comparisons
cause petty men confusion.
Jade from Jīng used to strike at magpies—
truly fearing the misuse of precious treasure;
dragon-pool jade carved into shapes—
is it not merely a waste of divine thought?
When Carpenter Shí turns his gaze,
rotten timber becomes carved beams;
with Sūn Yáng’s single word,
galloping hooves turn into noble steeds.
Thus I know that borrowing another’s praise
is weightier than connecting cities;
borrowing another’s feathers
brings more honor than a foot of jade.
The dark sea stretches ninety thousand miles,
yet cannot surpass the depth of this grace;
Mount Huà rises five thousand ren,
yet ultimately feels ashamed before the weight of this kindness.
Now, the golden gate's slender pipes,
have not yet stirred the spring ashes;
the stone wall's faint thunder,
still conceals winter's dormancy.
I humbly pray that Your Majesty's person,
may timely embrace ease and joy.
The precious pheasant of Nányáng,
is fortunate enough to be admired;
the chrysanthemum spring of Lìxiàn,
can somewhat prolong life.
I humbly await the day when arrival at Yè is expected,
and following to Liáng has its date.
Together in the alliance meeting like Qǐzǐ,
I am sure to gaze upon the dust of your carriage;
accompanying Lord Xuē in coming to court,
I shall respectfully welcome your capped and canopied entourage.
Fish-intestine thin silk,
phoenix-feet several lines,
writing these words of thanks,
I know in the end they are insufficient.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, chapter 656.
“Reply to Prince Zhào’s Letter”
I respectfully state:
I have learned that you have spread your tent over all of Hán,
and connected camps on the upper lands.
Deploying formations at Miǎnchí,
you lifted the siege of Dèng Yǔ;
opening the gates of Hángǔ Pass,
you stripped the seal of Wáng Yuán.
Bee-emblazoned banners raised at dawn,
clanging watchmen’s bells at night,
greatly embolden the hearts of warriors,
and fully rouse the ambition to march unhindered.
Moreover, a talented lady has gone forth in marriage,
and gained a worthy husband;
outside the frontier there is a city of the lady,
within the army there is the spirit of women.
The commandant’s blue banners,
bring instant spring colors;
the general’s great tree,
has already bloomed again.
Cloudy mists float over the ramparts,
shooting stars glide past the pillows.
Graceful dances and long songs,
horizontal flutes and vertical pipes.
At this very moment,
upon the azure clouds.
I, Xìn, unlearned and without skill,
by nature sunk in mud,
suddenly encountered Heaven’s favor,
searching out and promoting the lowly and obscure;
now I am appointed to oversee the judicial office,
and participate in the engraving of the tripods.
The penal codes of the new year,
should already be suspended;
the wooden clapper of early spring,
is just in need of a herald.
But my hair has already turned autumn-hued,
my spirit and wit long exhausted;
the auspicious stone and the lung stone,
cannot be measured;
the tip of my tongue and the tip of my brush,
only know congestion and obstruction.
Missing the chance to meet for a month,
has thus spanned two years;
tilting my head to gaze eastward,
mountains and rivers stretch a thousand *lǐ*.
The dust of travel not yet settled,
frost and dew moisten my clothes;
I look up wishing you to treasure your well-being,
and consider it the treasure of your person.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, chapter 665.
“Thanks for Prince Zhào Showing New Poems”
I respectfully state:
Zhèng Ruì has arrived,
bearing your handwritten instruction spanning several sheets,
and showing new poems.
The eight styles and six scripts,
are enough to startle brush and ink;
the four beginnings and six principles,
truly stir the spirit.
Lofty and elevated in diction,
ethereal and far-reaching in meaning,
the writing, unlike water, yet gushes like a spring;
the brush, though not autumn, hangs dew.
If hidden in mountain cliffs,
it could cause clouds and mists to rise densely;
if ferried on river banks,
it must make dragons coil around the boat.
Early summer is clear and mild,
Your Majesty’s person is joyful and at ease.
Glazed vermilion tubes,
magpies look back and phoenixes circle;
gracefully turning dark green,
apes are startled and geese fall.
Beneath your influence, I bow my head,
counting days as years.
The Gentleman of Jiānwéi,
truly has sincere wishes;
the Registrar of Bìjī,
has no way to fulfill his heart.
Lonely is my bramble door,
overgrown and neglected the orchid path;
your carriage coming to Liáng,
I have not yet divined the date;
dispatch riders to Yè,
I hope you will deign to take a detour.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, chapter 856.
“Thanks for Prince Zhào Bestowing Silk, Cloth, etc.”
I respectfully state:
Zhèng Ruì has arrived,
and I received the gracious gift of silk, cloth, damask, etc., ten bolts.
Wáng Bāo has arrived,
and I further received the promise of a gift of money, etc.
Grace beyond expectation,
truly matches a great bestowal;
an extraordinary conferral,
overflows my livelihood.
Dragging the fine silk to view it,
I need not labor to gaze at white horses;
wishing to entrust myself to flowing springs,
I stand waiting to see the blue wild ducks fly.
Dredging the pond to dig up lotus roots,
moving trees in Lǐ’s garden,
I rejoice in the valley’s profit,
and even more think of the green wood.
Chénliù’s stored grain,
puts me to shame for such deep kindness;
Lìyáng’s raining gold,
makes me blush for such generous favor.
A long-time guest at the Spiritual Terrace,
from now on I can count on cooking;
the long cold of Shǔ Valley,
from this day becomes warmer.
Even with the fields of Yúnmèng,
one could not surpass this joy;
even obtaining the sword of Fēngchéng,
would not equal this delight.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, chapter 655.
“Thanks for Prince Zhào Bestowing Silk and Cloth”
I respectfully state:
I have received your instruction and the gracious bestowal of variegated silk and cloth, thirty bolts.
Last winter was frozen and shut,
this spring is severe and harsh;
sleet like jade fields,
ice like salt flats.
Zhāng Chāo’s walls,
would not suffice to block the wind;
Yuán Ān’s door,
had no one to open the snow.
Covered with bird feathers yet not warm,
burning beast-shaped charcoal only increases the cold.
From afar you descended with holy compassion,
bending down in pity to relieve.
Speaking of the silkworm month,
nearly exhausted the mulberry carts;
the ferry truly held the shuttles,
almost emptying the weaving chambers.
Thus it makes the new market’s coin counters,
suddenly suspect they are selling colored silk;
the moonlit night of Pínglíng,
startled to hear the pounding of clothes.
A concubine encountering new fine silk,
naturally feels subdued in heart;
a wife hearing the tearing of silk,
will surely break into smiles.
Zhuāng Zhōu’s carriage ruts,
truly had parched fish;
Lord Xìnlíng’s whip before,
originally was no destitute bird.
Looking up, I receive your succor and aid,
bowing, I bear your deep kindness.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, chapter 655.
“Thanks for Prince Zhào Bestowing Silk and Cloth”
I, so-and-so, respectfully submit:
My son Gǒuniáng,
recently graced by Your Excellency’s summons,
was generously bestowed with five bolts of silk and cloth, among other gifts.
A southern captive granted pardon,
he was already included in the ceremonial reception;
a child barely old enough to wear proper robes,
he was further honored with an audience.
The weaving from Guānyǐn’s ferry bridge,
the double-threaded silk of Yè;
the patterned loom of Fúfēng,
the solitary cocoon from the immortal garden.
The blue collar should be worn,
the scholar not abandoning his studies’ verses;
the spring garments now complete,
the child may dance in the Yú and Yí rites.
Moreover, the nesting crow with its fledgling,
together knows the grace of the cassia tree;
the marsh pheasant leading its chicks,
shares joy in the spring-promoting decree.
When the roots receive moisture,
branches and leaves alike flourish.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks for the White Silk Robe and Trousers Bestowed by the Prince of Zhào”
“Letter of Thanks for the White Silk Robe and Trousers Bestowed by the Prince of Zhào”
I, so-and-so, respectfully submit:
You have bestowed a set of white silk robe and trousers.
Chéng Jù presented a memorial,
merely discussing pheasant-head silk;
Wáng Gōng entered the snow,
vainly praised crane-feather cloak.
Never before has there been such a clever loom and intricate weave,
transforming into wondrous patterns,
where phoenixes seem ever soaring without departing,
and flowers, though cold, never wither.
Wearing this, a thousand-gold warmth briefly felt,
abandoning the hundred-patched enduring chill,
forever free from sighs over yellow ramie,
now witnessing the esteem of blue damask.
Facing Tiānshān’s accumulated snow,
one may still open the collar;
braving Guǎnglè’s long winds,
one ought to wipe away sweat.
The white turtle repaying its master,
in the end knows no deadline;
the yellow sparrow thanking kindness,
when will it ever know the day?
○From *Yìwén Lèijù*, scroll 85.
From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks for the Headscarf Bestowed by the Prince of Téng”
I, so-and-so, respectfully submit:
By your instruction,
you bestowed a deer-pattern headscarf.
Newly shed antlers,
freshly sprouted vines.
Falling stars intermingling in reflection,
scattered pearls sparsely dotted.
The coiling dragon’s shears have cut it,
the long-life threads still sewn.
Kingfisher feathers are surely surpassed,
lotus blossoms highly yield.
Wandering as a recluse,
it suffices to mock drum-skin caps;
entering spring woods,
one may boast of bamboo-shoot sheaths.
My disheveled hair, unkempt and loose,
aging face, withered and decayed,
unwashed for three autumns,
truly bears your present grace;
once in ten years a headgear,
all the more delights in this gift.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks for Silk, Cloth, and Other Items Bestowed by the Enlightened Emperor”
“Letter of Thanks for Silk, Cloth, and Other Items Bestowed by the Enlightened Emperor”
I, your subject so-and-so, respectfully submit:
By imperial decree, you bestowed thirty bolts of assorted silk, cloth, floss, and gauze, along with two hundred coins in silver.
In recent years,
I have been particularly lacking.
Within the White Society’s grounds,
brushing grass to view ice;
inside the Spiritual Terrace,
blowing dust to inspect the cauldron.
Resentful wife and harsh concubine,
both sighing and detesting;
emaciated sons and frail grandsons,
hollow courtesy, true grievance.
The royal envoy suddenly descended,
great bounty arrived first.
The Celestial Emperor granting years,
none surpass this joy;
immortal lad presenting medicine,
cannot equal this delight.
Spreading sleeves to dance,
dark cranes wish to come;
keeping rhythm to sing,
passing clouds nearly break.
So-called boat without shore,
Hǎiruò for it reverses winds;
shepherd’s purse and wheat about to wither,
mountain spirits for it bring forth rain.
Moreover, fully drawn plain cocoons,
snowy slopes seem to pour;
together fallen green ducks,
silver mountains perhaps stir.
Thus knowing the green-ox Daoist,
further extends a life nearing its end;
the white-deer immortal,
can revive bones already dried.
Even if lifting mountains, crossing seas,
bearing virtue remains unmatched;
hanging dew, suspended needle,
writing gratitude never exhausts.
The Pénglái sparrow thanking kindness,
white jade, four rings;
the Hànshuǐ snake repaying virtue,
bright pearl, one inch.
I, observing this,
how could be without ashamed heart!
Simply because things receive their life,
from Heaven, no thanks needed.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks for the Rhinoceros-Horn Belt and Other Items Bestowed by the Prince of Zhào”
I, so-and-so, respectfully submit:
By your instruction,
you bestowed a rhinoceros-horn adorned belt and ten strings of cash.
Lord Wèi’s precious belt,
specially granted to Liú Zhēn;
the Prince of Zhào’s state taxes,
partially aided Péi Kǎi.
Strung hidden-pattern horse,
like burning Ānxī silver;
belt set with pierced rhinoceros horn,
resembling hunting Yúnnán beast.
Běiguō Sāo’s enduring poverty,
is what I gladly accept;
Nángōng Jìng’s loaded treasures,
truly not my aspiration.
Flowers blooming in four directions,
only see their glory;
giant turtle bearing three mountains,
deeply know its weight.
Formerly Shěn Xī about to perish,
met the Director of Fate and returned to life;
Shì Xiè being buried,
encountered an immortal and revived.
Today’s compassionate mercy,
this is what it means!
Horse leading before to guide the way,
perhaps seems to recognize kindness;
rooster before dawn opening the gate,
may be able to repay the master.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks for the Rice Bestowed by the Prince of Zhào”
I, so-and-so, respectfully submit:
By your instruction, you bestowed ten dàn of rice.
Red bird carrying ear of grain,
already gathered in Western Zhōu;
yellow sparrow following cart,
returned flying to Eastern Market.
Soaked to become seed,
not without frost and snow’s essence;
taken to discuss warfare,
immediately has mountains and rivers’ momentum.
I, in humble lane with bamboo bowl and gourd ladle,
combing wind, bathing rain,
peeling elm bark in autumn frontier,
digging hibernating swallows on cold hills.
Looking up, consuming state taxes,
thus opening dusty cauldron,
not alchemical furnace flowing pearls,
different from Jīngtái cooking jade.
Dōngfāng Shuò holding rice,
already ceased long hunger;
Xīmén Bào reclaiming fields,
truly shamed by this gift.
○From *Yìwén Lèijù*, scroll 72.
From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks for the Dried Fish Bestowed by the Prince of Zhào”
I respectfully submit:
I have received your gift of ten dried fish.
In the morning they float upon the Lǐ waters,
their brilliance resembling crimson turtles;
at night they touch like the patterned yáo fish,
their fins akin to azure phoenixes.
Moreover, these are the fresh crucian carp of Dòngtíng,
the fine bream of Wēn Lake,
whose scales churn waves into rain,
and whose armor wards off the cold.
I, originally a man of Wú,
have often longed for the flavors of rivers and lakes;
yet in my hunger,
I have only relied on the remnants of wild greens.
Your compassionate gift is a profound kindness,
rich fats flowing to my stove.
Without toiling at the Lion Pavilion,
it already surpasses the bounty of Léichí.
It startles even the River Earl,
who alone receives no offerings from men;
it is enough to laugh at Rén Gōng,
who spent his years angling in vain.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks to Prince Téng for the Gift of a Horse”
I respectfully submit:
By your instruction, I have received the gift of a black-maned horse.
Before Liǔgǔ’s mine opened,
I unexpectedly encountered a purple swallow;
while distant from Língyuán’s source,
I suddenly behold peach blossoms.
Its flowing lightning vies in radiance,
its floating clouds link with shadows.
In leisure moments like Zhāng Chǎng painting eyebrows,
it will gallop straight to Zhāngtái;
in joyous revelry like Wáng Jì drinking wine,
it will charge down the golden track.
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Yìwén Lèijù*, scroll 93.
Also in *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks to Prince Téng for the Gift of a Pig”
I respectfully submit:
By your instruction, I have received the gift of a plump pig.
Its white head deemed precious,
it crossed the waters of Liáodōng;
valued for its red markings,
it faced the walls of Xiāngyáng.
Suddenly bestowed in full grace,
I shall respectfully prepare it for roasting.
Sūn Hóng herded by the Zī River,
only seeking coins;
Bǔ Shì raised them in Shànglín,
how could he know their flavor?
Respectfully submitted.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
“Letter of Thanks to Prince Zhào for the Gift of a Horse and an Umbrella”
I respectfully submit:
By your instruction, I have received the gift of a purple-maned horse,
along with silver-studded riding gear and a purple silk umbrella.
Heaven sends down rain,
specially bestowing deep favor;
the Ruò River’s flowing light,
uniquely grants private illumination.
This emerald canopy bestowed,
rivals the kindness Liú Jī received;
this black steed conferred,
surpasses the honor of Lǐ Zhōng’s gift.
The red curtains of the northern ministry,
shall now be rolled high;
the bamboo horse of Xīhé,
already greets it in the suburbs.
My life is as light,
as a goose feather floating on Ruò Water;
knowing the weight of your grace,
as a turtle bearing Líng Mountain.
Moreover, like a startled swan leaving water,
only seeing its lingering;
a yellow crane departing the pass,
only knowing to look back.
My heart of attachment and longing,
is just the same as this.
○From *Wényuàn Yīnghuá*, scroll 655.
